label: Severe-range blood pressure
message: Recheck in 15 minutes. If it stays this high, treat urgently (e.g. labetalol / nifedipine as per protocol) and assess for severe pre-eclampsia, or refer.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 160 mmHg

label: Severe-range blood pressure
message: Recheck in 15 minutes. If it stays this high, treat urgently (e.g. labetalol / nifedipine as per protocol) and assess for severe pre-eclampsia, or refer.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 110 mmHg

label: Possible pre-eclampsia
message: Raised BP with protein in the urine after 20 weeks. Assess the same day: symptoms (headache, visual change, epigastric pain), platelets, liver and kidney tests; plan monitoring or admission.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 140 mmHg and Urine albumin 1+ or more, from 20 weeks

label: Possible pre-eclampsia
message: Raised BP with protein in the urine after 20 weeks. Assess the same day: symptoms (headache, visual change, epigastric pain), platelets, liver and kidney tests; plan monitoring or admission.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 90 mmHg and Urine albumin 1+ or more, from 20 weeks

label: Raised blood pressure
message: BP 140/90 or more. Recheck after rest; if confirmed, check urine protein and follow up closely (gestational or chronic hypertension).
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 140 mmHg and BP systolic under 160 mmHg

label: Raised blood pressure
message: BP 140/90 or more. Recheck after rest; if confirmed, check urine protein and follow up closely (gestational or chronic hypertension).
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 90 mmHg and BP diastolic under 110 mmHg

label: Severe anaemia
message: Hb below 7 g/dL. Needs urgent assessment and treatment in hospital (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for the cause.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Hb under 7 g/dL

label: Moderate anaemia
message: Hb 7–9.9 g/dL. Start treatment-dose iron (consider IV iron, especially later in pregnancy or if oral iron is not tolerated) and recheck Hb.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Hb at least 7 g/dL and Hb under 10 g/dL

label: Mild anaemia
message: Hb 10–10.9 g/dL. Treatment-dose oral iron and folic acid; recheck Hb in about 4 weeks.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Hb at least 10 g/dL and Hb under 11 g/dL

label: Reduced or absent fetal movements
message: Check the fetal heart now and arrange a CTG (and ultrasound if needed) the same day.
source: RCOG Green-top 57 Reduced fetal movements; NICE NG229 / FIGO intrapartum fetal monitoring (normal FHR 110–160)
text: Fetal movements: reduced or absent, from 28 weeks

label: Slow fetal heart rate
message: Fetal heart rate below 110/min. Recheck for a full minute and arrange CTG / urgent assessment.
source: RCOG Green-top 57 Reduced fetal movements; NICE NG229 / FIGO intrapartum fetal monitoring (normal FHR 110–160)
text: Fetal heart rate under 110 /min

label: Fast fetal heart rate
message: Fetal heart rate above 160/min. Recheck for a full minute, check maternal temperature and pulse, and arrange CTG / urgent assessment.
source: RCOG Green-top 57 Reduced fetal movements; NICE NG229 / FIGO intrapartum fetal monitoring (normal FHR 110–160)
text: Fetal heart rate over 160 /min

label: Low oxygen saturation
message: SpO₂ below 95%. Recheck; assess breathing and arrange urgent medical review.
source: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (2016); MoHFW India MCP card danger signs
text: SpO₂ under 95 %

label: Fever
message: Temperature 100.4 °F or more. Look for the cause (urine infection, malaria, dengue, respiratory infection, chorioamnionitis) and treat.
source: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (2016); MoHFW India MCP card danger signs
text: Temperature at least 100.4 °F

label: Fast maternal pulse
message: Pulse above 110/min. Look for anaemia, infection, bleeding, dehydration or heart disease.
source: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience (2016); MoHFW India MCP card danger signs
text: Pulse over 110 /min

label: Sugar in urine
message: Arrange a blood glucose test (75 g OGTT, DIPSI) if not already done.
source: FOGSI GCPR Gestational diabetes mellitus (2018); MoHFW India National guidelines for diagnosis and management of GDM (2018)
text: Urine sugar 1+ or more

label: Marked oedema
message: Check BP and urine protein for pre-eclampsia.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: Oedema moderate or more, from 20 weeks

label: Not head-down at term
message: Confirm by ultrasound and discuss options (external cephalic version or planned mode of delivery).
source: RCOG Green-top 20a/20b (breech); FOGSI GCPR
text: Presentation: breech or transverse or oblique, from 36 weeks

label: Fundal height not matching the weeks
message: Fundal height differs from the weeks by more than 3 cm. Consider a growth scan (growth restriction, too much or too little fluid, twins, or wrong dates).
source: RCOG Green-top 31 Small-for-gestational-age fetus; WHO ANC 2016 (symphysis-fundal height)
text: Fundal height differs from weeks by over 3 cm, 24–40 weeks

label: Sudden weight gain
message: More than 1 kg a week since the last weighed visit. Check BP, urine protein and oedema (fluid retention / pre-eclampsia).
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: Weight gain since last visit over 1 kg/week, from 20 weeks

label: 41 weeks or more
message: Plan delivery (induction of labour) as per the hospital protocol if she has not delivered; check fetal wellbeing.
source: WHO recommendations for induction of labour (2011, 2022); FOGSI GCPR Induction of labour
text: Weeks of pregnancy today at least 41 weeks

label: Severe anaemia
message: Hb below 7 g/dL. Needs urgent assessment and treatment in hospital (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for the cause.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Haemoglobin (lab) under 7 g/dL

label: Moderate anaemia
message: Hb 7–9.9 g/dL. Start treatment-dose iron (consider IV iron, especially later in pregnancy or if oral iron is not tolerated) and recheck Hb.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Haemoglobin (lab) at least 7 g/dL and Haemoglobin (lab) under 10 g/dL

label: Mild anaemia
message: Hb 10–10.9 g/dL. Treatment-dose oral iron and folic acid; recheck Hb in about 4 weeks.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Haemoglobin (lab) at least 10 g/dL and Haemoglobin (lab) under 11 g/dL

label: Platelets below normal
message: Platelets 1–1.49 lakh/µL. Often gestational thrombocytopenia: check BP, repeat the count, and look for other causes if it falls.
source: ACOG Practice Bulletin 207 Thrombocytopenia in pregnancy (2019); ACOG Practice Bulletin 222 Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia (2020); FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: Platelets (lab) at least 1 lakh/µL and Platelets (lab) under 1.5 lakh/µL

label: Gestational diabetes range (OGTT)
message: 2-hour glucose 140–199 mg/dL after 75 g glucose. Start diet advice and glucose monitoring as per the GDM protocol; treat if the targets are not met.
source: MoHFW India National guidelines for diagnosis and management of GDM (2018, DIPSI test: 2-hour value 140 mg/dL or more); FOGSI GCPR Gestational diabetes mellitus (2018)
text: OGTT 2-hour blood sugar (lab) at least 140 mg/dL and OGTT 2-hour blood sugar (lab) under 200 mg/dL

label: Diabetes range (OGTT)
message: 2-hour glucose 200 mg/dL or more after 75 g glucose: diabetes in pregnancy. Start treatment without delay and involve a physician.
source: WHO Diagnostic criteria and classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy (2013); MoHFW India National guidelines for diagnosis and management of GDM (2018, DIPSI test: 2-hour value 140 mg/dL or more); FOGSI GCPR Gestational diabetes mellitus (2018)
text: OGTT 2-hour blood sugar (lab) at least 200 mg/dL

label: Raised fasting blood sugar
message: Fasting glucose 92–125 mg/dL: gestational diabetes range. Confirm as per the hospital protocol (75 g test) and start diet advice.
source: WHO Diagnostic criteria and classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy (2013); FOGSI GCPR Gestational diabetes mellitus (2018)
text: Fasting blood sugar (lab) at least 92 mg/dL and Fasting blood sugar (lab) under 126 mg/dL

label: Diabetes range (fasting sugar)
message: Fasting glucose 126 mg/dL or more: diabetes in pregnancy. Start treatment without delay and involve a physician.
source: WHO Diagnostic criteria and classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy (2013)
text: Fasting blood sugar (lab) at least 126 mg/dL

label: Diabetes range (random sugar)
message: Random glucose 200 mg/dL or more. Confirm with a fasting or 75 g test and start treatment; check urine ketones if she is unwell.
source: WHO Diagnostic criteria and classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy (2013)
text: Random blood sugar (lab) at least 200 mg/dL

label: Raised TSH
message: TSH above 4 µIU/mL. Check free T4 (and TPO antibodies if available) and treat hypothyroidism as per guideline; TSH above 10 needs treatment whatever the free T4. The Government of India guideline uses lower limits (2.5 in the first trimester, 3 later) – use your own range if the hospital has one.
source: American Thyroid Association guidelines for thyroid disease during pregnancy and the postpartum (2017); MoHFW India National guidelines for screening of hypothyroidism during pregnancy (2014)
text: TSH (lab) over 4 µIU/mL

label: Low TSH
message: TSH below 0.1 µIU/mL. Often normal in early pregnancy (hCG effect, severe vomiting): check free T4 and look for signs of thyrotoxicosis.
source: American Thyroid Association guidelines for thyroid disease during pregnancy and the postpartum (2017); MoHFW India National guidelines for screening of hypothyroidism during pregnancy (2014)
text: TSH (lab) under 0.1 µIU/mL

label: Protein in urine (lab result)
message: Albumin 1+ or more in the lab urine test after 20 weeks. Check BP today for pre-eclampsia; rule out urine infection; consider a urine protein : creatinine ratio.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: Urine albumin (lab) 1+ or more, from 20 weeks

label: Possible pre-eclampsia
message: Raised BP with protein in a lab urine test of the same week (within 7 days), after 20 weeks. Assess the same day: symptoms (headache, visual change, epigastric pain), platelets, liver and kidney tests; plan monitoring or admission.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 140 mmHg and Urine albumin (lab) 1+ or more, from 20 weeks, values recorded within 7 days of each other

label: Possible pre-eclampsia
message: Raised BP with protein in a lab urine test of the same week (within 7 days), after 20 weeks. Assess the same day: symptoms (headache, visual change, epigastric pain), platelets, liver and kidney tests; plan monitoring or admission.
source: FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019); WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia (2011); NICE NG133 (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 90 mmHg and Urine albumin (lab) 1+ or more, from 20 weeks, values recorded within 7 days of each other

label: Low platelets
message: Platelets below 1 lakh/µL. Check BP and liver tests for HELLP or severe pre-eclampsia, repeat the count, and plan delivery, anaesthesia and bleeding risk with the physician.
source: ACOG Practice Bulletin 207 Thrombocytopenia in pregnancy (2019); ACOG Practice Bulletin 222 Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia (2020); FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: Platelets (lab) under 1 lakh/µL

label: Severe-range blood pressure after delivery
message: BP 160/110 or more after delivery. Recheck in 15 minutes; if it stays this high, treat urgently as per protocol and assess for pre-eclampsia or eclampsia, which can begin after delivery.
source: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience (2022); NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (2019), postnatal care; FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 160 mmHg

label: Severe-range blood pressure after delivery
message: BP 160/110 or more after delivery. Recheck in 15 minutes; if it stays this high, treat urgently as per protocol and assess for pre-eclampsia or eclampsia, which can begin after delivery.
source: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience (2022); NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (2019), postnatal care; FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 110 mmHg

label: Raised blood pressure after delivery
message: BP 140/90 or more after delivery. Recheck after rest; ask about headache, visual change and upper abdominal pain; check urine protein and follow up closely.
source: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience (2022); NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (2019), postnatal care; FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: BP systolic at least 140 mmHg and BP systolic under 160 mmHg

label: Raised blood pressure after delivery
message: BP 140/90 or more after delivery. Recheck after rest; ask about headache, visual change and upper abdominal pain; check urine protein and follow up closely.
source: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience (2022); NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (2019), postnatal care; FOGSI GCPR Hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (2019)
text: BP diastolic at least 90 mmHg and BP diastolic under 110 mmHg

label: Fever after delivery
message: Temperature 100.4 °F (38 °C) or more after delivery. Look for infection – uterus, wound or perineum, breast, urine, chest – and for sepsis; treat or refer the same day.
source: WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of maternal peripartum infections (2015); WHO postnatal care recommendations (2022); MoHFW India SBA guidelines (danger signs after delivery)
text: Temperature at least 100.4 °F

label: Fast pulse after delivery
message: Pulse above 110/min after delivery. Check BP, bleeding, the uterus, temperature and Hb: a fast pulse can be the first sign of blood loss or infection.
source: WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): a fast pulse (110/min or more) is a sign of shock – this draft rule is raised over 110, like the pregnancy rule; change it to "at least 110" to follow WHO exactly. WHO postnatal care recommendations (2022)
text: Pulse over 110 /min

label: Severe anaemia after delivery
message: Hb below 7 g/dL after delivery. Needs urgent assessment and treatment (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for continuing bleeding.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Hb under 7 g/dL

label: Severe anaemia after delivery
message: Hb below 7 g/dL after delivery. Needs urgent assessment and treatment (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for continuing bleeding.
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Haemoglobin (lab) under 7 g/dL

label: Very low temperature (baby)
message: Temperature below 95.9 °F (35.5 °C). Rewarm now and assess for serious infection and low blood sugar; admit or refer.
source: WHO Thermal protection of the newborn: a practical guide (1997) – normal 36.5–37.5 °C, so a temperature above 37.5 °C is raised; MoHFW India IMNCI and Facility Based Newborn Care – below 35.5 °C is a danger sign. IMNCI counts 37.5 °C itself as fever: change "over 99.5" to "at least 99.5" to follow IMNCI exactly
text: Temperature under 95.9 °F

label: Low temperature (baby)
message: Temperature below 97.7 °F (36.5 °C). Warm the baby – skin-to-skin, cap, warm room – and recheck within an hour; check feeding and blood sugar.
source: WHO Thermal protection of the newborn: a practical guide (1997) – normal 36.5–37.5 °C, so a temperature above 37.5 °C is raised; MoHFW India IMNCI and Facility Based Newborn Care – below 35.5 °C is a danger sign. IMNCI counts 37.5 °C itself as fever: change "over 99.5" to "at least 99.5" to follow IMNCI exactly
text: Temperature at least 95.9 °F and Temperature under 97.7 °F

label: High temperature (baby)
message: Temperature above 99.5 °F (37.5 °C). Check for over-wrapping and measure again; if it stays high, assess for infection the same day – fever in a young baby is a danger sign.
source: WHO Thermal protection of the newborn: a practical guide (1997) – normal 36.5–37.5 °C, so a temperature above 37.5 °C is raised; MoHFW India IMNCI and Facility Based Newborn Care – below 35.5 °C is a danger sign. IMNCI counts 37.5 °C itself as fever: change "over 99.5" to "at least 99.5" to follow IMNCI exactly
text: Temperature over 99.5 °F

label: Weight more than 10 % below birth weight
message: Assess the baby for dehydration, jaundice and illness, watch a feed and support feeding; recheck the weight in 24–48 hours.
source: NICE NG75 Faltering growth (2017), recommendation 1.1.2; MoHFW India Facility Based Newborn Care (weight loss in the first week up to 10 % of the birth weight)
text: Weight below birth weight by over 10 %

label: High bilirubin for the baby's age
message: Total bilirubin above 5.8 mg/dL in the first 24 hours of life. This is the NICE line for starting phototherapy at the start of that day, for a baby born at 38 weeks or later. Plot the value on the hour-specific chart now and treat if it is above the line. A baby born before 38 weeks, or with risk factors, needs treatment at lower values, which this rule does not check.
source: NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (2010, updated 2023): treatment threshold table for babies of 38 weeks or more (100, 200, 250, 300 and 350 µmol/L at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours of age); hour-specific charts: AAP 2022, NNF India
text: Baby's total bilirubin (lab) over 5.8 mg/dL, baby under 1 day old

label: High bilirubin for the baby's age
message: Total bilirubin above 11.7 mg/dL at 24–47 hours of age. This is the NICE line for starting phototherapy at the start of that day, for a baby born at 38 weeks or later. Plot the value on the hour-specific chart now and treat if it is above the line. A baby born before 38 weeks, or with risk factors, needs treatment at lower values, which this rule does not check.
source: NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (2010, updated 2023): treatment threshold table for babies of 38 weeks or more (100, 200, 250, 300 and 350 µmol/L at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours of age); hour-specific charts: AAP 2022, NNF India
text: Baby's total bilirubin (lab) over 11.7 mg/dL, baby 1 day old

label: High bilirubin for the baby's age
message: Total bilirubin above 14.6 mg/dL at 48–71 hours of age. This is the NICE line for starting phototherapy at the start of that day, for a baby born at 38 weeks or later. Plot the value on the hour-specific chart now and treat if it is above the line. A baby born before 38 weeks, or with risk factors, needs treatment at lower values, which this rule does not check.
source: NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (2010, updated 2023): treatment threshold table for babies of 38 weeks or more (100, 200, 250, 300 and 350 µmol/L at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours of age); hour-specific charts: AAP 2022, NNF India
text: Baby's total bilirubin (lab) over 14.6 mg/dL, baby 2 days old

label: High bilirubin for the baby's age
message: Total bilirubin above 17.5 mg/dL at 72–95 hours of age. This is the NICE line for starting phototherapy at the start of that day, for a baby born at 38 weeks or later. Plot the value on the hour-specific chart now and treat if it is above the line. A baby born before 38 weeks, or with risk factors, needs treatment at lower values, which this rule does not check.
source: NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (2010, updated 2023): treatment threshold table for babies of 38 weeks or more (100, 200, 250, 300 and 350 µmol/L at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours of age); hour-specific charts: AAP 2022, NNF India
text: Baby's total bilirubin (lab) over 17.5 mg/dL, baby 3 days old

label: High bilirubin for the baby's age
message: Total bilirubin above 20.5 mg/dL at 96 hours of age or later. This is the NICE line for starting phototherapy at the start of that day, for a baby born at 38 weeks or later. Plot the value on the hour-specific chart now and treat if it is above the line. A baby born before 38 weeks, or with risk factors, needs treatment at lower values, which this rule does not check.
source: NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (2010, updated 2023): treatment threshold table for babies of 38 weeks or more (100, 200, 250, 300 and 350 µmol/L at 0, 24, 48, 72 and 96 hours of age); hour-specific charts: AAP 2022, NNF India
text: Baby's total bilirubin (lab) over 20.5 mg/dL, baby 4 days old or more

label: Raised direct bilirubin (baby)
message: Direct (conjugated) bilirubin above 1.0 mg/dL. Conjugated jaundice is never normal: ask about pale stools and dark urine and arrange evaluation for cholestasis (for example biliary atresia) without delay.
source: NASPGHAN / ESPGHAN guideline for the evaluation of cholestatic jaundice in infants (2017): direct bilirubin above 1.0 mg/dL is abnormal
text: Baby's direct bilirubin (lab) over 1 mg/dL

label: Low blood sugar (baby)
message: Blood glucose below 45 mg/dL. Feed now and recheck in 30–60 minutes as per the hospital protocol; a baby with symptoms or a very low value needs IV glucose.
source: NNF India Clinical Practice Guidelines: Management of neonatal hypoglycaemia (2010) – operational threshold: plasma glucose below 45 mg/dL
text: Baby's blood sugar (lab) under 45 mg/dL

label: Possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy
message: An ectopic pregnancy, or a pregnancy not yet located, with a pulse over 110/min. Consider a ruptured ectopic pregnancy with bleeding inside the abdomen. Assess now: pain, pallor, abdominal tenderness, shoulder-tip pain; two IV lines, blood for cross-match, and surgery without delay if she is unstable. A miscarriage with heavy bleeding can look the same. (NICE NG126; RCOG GTG 21)
source: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023); RCOG Green-top Guideline 21 Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy (2016); WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): a fast pulse (110/min or more) and systolic BP below 90 mmHg are signs of shock
text: Pregnancy location: ectopic or unknown and Pulse over 110 /min

label: Possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy
message: An ectopic pregnancy, or a pregnancy not yet located, with systolic BP below 90 mmHg. Consider a ruptured ectopic pregnancy with bleeding inside the abdomen. Assess now: pain, pallor, abdominal tenderness, shoulder-tip pain; two IV lines, blood for cross-match, and surgery without delay if she is unstable. A miscarriage with heavy bleeding can look the same. (NICE NG126; RCOG GTG 21)
source: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023); RCOG Green-top Guideline 21 Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy (2016); WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): a fast pulse (110/min or more) and systolic BP below 90 mmHg are signs of shock
text: Pregnancy location: ectopic or unknown and BP systolic under 90 mmHg

label: Possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy
message: Signs of rupture are recorded on her record. Consider a ruptured ectopic pregnancy with bleeding inside the abdomen. Assess now: pain, pallor, abdominal tenderness, shoulder-tip pain; two IV lines, blood for cross-match, and surgery without delay if she is unstable. A miscarriage with heavy bleeding can look the same. (NICE NG126; RCOG GTG 21)
source: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023); RCOG Green-top Guideline 21 Diagnosis and management of ectopic pregnancy (2016); WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): a fast pulse (110/min or more) and systolic BP below 90 mmHg are signs of shock
text: Signs of rupture: yes

label: Possible septic abortion
message: Temperature 100.4 °F (38 °C) or more with a pulse over 110/min after a pregnancy loss. Consider a septic abortion (infection of the uterus). Assess now: BP, breathing, abdominal and uterine tenderness, the discharge; start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and fluids without delay and plan to empty the uterus if tissue remains. (WHO MCPC 2017; RCOG GTG 64a)
source: WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): septic abortion; RCOG Green-top Guideline 64a Bacterial sepsis in pregnancy (2012); FOGSI
text: Temperature at least 100.4 °F and Pulse over 110 /min

label: Possible septic abortion
message: Fever with foul-smelling discharge is recorded on her record. Consider a septic abortion (infection of the uterus). Assess now: BP, breathing, abdominal and uterine tenderness, the discharge; start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and fluids without delay and plan to empty the uterus if tissue remains. (WHO MCPC 2017; RCOG GTG 64a)
source: WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): septic abortion; RCOG Green-top Guideline 64a Bacterial sepsis in pregnancy (2012); FOGSI
text: Fever with foul-smelling discharge: yes

label: Heavy bleeding
message: Heavy bleeding is recorded on her record. Check pulse, BP and Hb now; look for tissue left in the uterus or at the cervix; resuscitate, and arrange evacuation or surgery as needed. (NICE NG126; WHO MCPC 2017)
source: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023); WHO Managing complications in pregnancy and childbirth (2nd edition, 2017): a fast pulse (110/min or more) and systolic BP below 90 mmHg are signs of shock
text: Bleeding: heavy

label: Severe anaemia after pregnancy loss
message: Hb below 7 g/dL. Needs urgent assessment and treatment (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for continuing bleeding. (WHO haemoglobin thresholds; Anemia Mukt Bharat)
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Hb under 7 g/dL

label: Severe anaemia after pregnancy loss
message: Hb below 7 g/dL. Needs urgent assessment and treatment (blood transfusion or IV iron as indicated); look for continuing bleeding. (WHO haemoglobin thresholds; Anemia Mukt Bharat)
source: WHO haemoglobin thresholds (2011, 2024); MoHFW India Anemia Mukt Bharat guidelines (2018); FOGSI GCPR Anaemia in pregnancy
text: Haemoglobin (lab) under 7 g/dL
